title: Root-space dimensions and independent Lie words
statement: For the generalized Cartan matrices and maximal contragredient quotient specified in records 532--533, compute a prescribed root-space dimension and independent representing words. No efficiency or canonical-basis requirement is present in the notebook.
status: As of November 2026: computationally determined degree by degree. Berman--Moody's 1979 formula covers symmetrizable matrices; the larger literal class is handled by finite recursive lowering maps as explained in the annotation. This is not recorded as an open demand for a uniform positive combinatorial formula. Earlier root-system and denominator occurrences are thematic predecessors, not exact previous formulations of this problem.

title: Three classical double-coset spaces
statement: Describe \(U(n)\backslash GL_n(\mathbb C)/U(n)\), \(B\backslash GL_n(\mathbb C)/B\), and \(U(n)\backslash GL_n(\mathbb C)/B\), with \(U(n)\) unitary and \(B\) the invertible upper triangular subgroup; the unitary interpretation is explicitly reconstructed.
status: As of November 2026: classical solved exercises. The invariants are respectively ordered positive singular values, a permutation in \(S_n\), and no invariant (one double coset). The three distinct questions share this problem entry. The earlier Bruhat occurrence 1979-483.1 is a related theorem, not an identical three-part question.

title: Integer Gelfand–Tsetlin arrays with four fixed top entries
statement: Count integer triangular interlacing arrays with fixed weakly increasing top row \(m_1,m_2,m_3,m_4\), including equality at every interlacing bound.
status: As of November 2026: solved by the type-A Weyl dimension product displayed in 1981-536.7 and the 1950 Gelfand--Tsetlin basis. The earlier 1976-415.5 and GP-1976-24 concern standard tableaux/Young-graph paths, a related but different branching graph; no exact recurrence of this fixed-integer-row question is present in the supplied index.

title: The type-A quiver formula for p-adic GL(n) multiplicities
statement: For standard induced representations of \(GL_n(F)\) on a fixed cuspidal line, express their irreducible Jordan--H\"older multiplicities through local intersection cohomology of the corresponding graded nilpotent/type-A quiver orbit closures. The notebook occurrence is an abbreviated allusion, identified through Zelevinsky's 1981 paper.
status: As of November 2026: proved in the specified GL(n) setting. Current direct sources are Solleveld's Theorem 5.4(b), his standard-module comparison Lemma 6.2, and Balodis's version-2 Theorem 3.9. First circulation and revision dates are separated in the occurrence. GP-1979-41 concerns the earlier Verma-module/Schubert Kazhdan--Lusztig problem; it is a related precursor, not this p-adic multiplicity question.

title: Kazhdan--Lusztig multiplicity and cohomological conjectures
statement: For ordinary Verma modules of a finite-dimensional complex semisimple Lie algebra, identify Jordan--Hölder multiplicities with Kazhdan--Lusztig values, and determine the coefficient refinements from local intersection cohomology and the Jantzen filtration with its correct grading.
status: As of November 2026, the ungraded theorem and geometric interpretation were already established before the November 1981 talk; the dominant-direction filtration refinement was proved in the 1993 Beilinson--Bernstein publication. Arbitrary-direction invariance is separately indexed as GP-1981-10, because it is false and has different quantifiers.

title: Dependence of Jantzen-layer multiplicities on deformation direction
statement: For a fixed regular-integral Verma module, are the multiplicities in each layer of the Jantzen filtration independent of the regular direction used to deform its highest weight?
status: As of November 2026: false without a dominant-cone restriction. Williamson, \S8.4, gives an explicit type-A3 example with a 13-dimensional weight space whose layer dimensions change from \((7,3,2,1)\) to \((7,2,4,0)\). First arXiv circulation was 8 October 2014; the journal volume is dated 2016 and its online release 7 July 2017. Dominant deformations satisfy the established Jantzen theorem. No unresolved residue is asserted for the literal seminar question.

title: Primitivity of enveloping algebras of algebraic Lie algebras
statement: Characterize finite-dimensional algebraic Lie algebras over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero whose universal enveloping algebra has a faithful simple module.
status: As of November 2026: already settled by the 1976 Ooms criterion, quoted exactly in Elashvili, \S0. Primitivity is equivalent to an open coadjoint orbit, equivalently a nondegenerate Kirillov form. Elashvili\textquotesingle s 1982 paper further classifies specified reduced semidirect-product families. The earlier supplied index gives no existing GP identifier for 1964-37.1, so a new problem ID is assigned while retaining its earlier occurrence.

title: Van der Pol relaxation limit and matching of slow branches
statement: Describe the limit as \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\) of the attracting periodic orbit of \(\varepsilon\ddot x+(x^2-1)\dot x+x=0\), including the connection of its slow branches by rapid transitions.
status: As of November 2026: established in the classical relaxation setting. Cartier\textquotesingle s November 1981 Bourbaki exposition, printed in 1982, gives a nonstandard-analysis treatment and the matched cycle. The notebook does not specify an additional unresolved initial-value, rate, or canard problem; those are not silently added.

title: Curvature actions with lower-order field equations
statement: Gelfand asks for curvature combinations whose metric Euler--Lagrange equations have lower order. A bounded precise version classifies natural symmetric divergence-free metric two-tensors of differential order at most two in fixed dimension and signature, modulo the separate issue of null Lagrangians. The unrestricted source wording is broader and lacks a specified class of actions.
status: As of November 2026, the reconstructed natural-tensor problem is solved by Lovelock's pre-1982 classification; \citet[Theorem 2.6]{navarronavarro2011lovelock} gives a verified exact formulation. The handwritten Einstein-and-Pontryagin answer is not a complete all-dimensional classification. Earlier Einstein-action discussions are thematic antecedents, not this definite classification question.

title: Convergence of the equations of Regge gravity
statement: For nondegenerate piecewise flat approximations of a smooth metric, determine a precise topology and geometric hypotheses under which the first variations or discrete Einstein equations converge. This must be separated from convergence of the curvature action and from convergence of actual solutions with fixed gauge and boundary data; the source specifies neither of the latter.
status: As of November 2026, \citet[Theorem 4.1 and Corollary 4.3 of the preprint]{gawlikneunteufel2023einstein} establish a rigorous positive-degree interpolant result for the distributional densitized Einstein tensor in \(H^{-2}\). This is a partial resolution of a specified consistency problem. No general convergence theorem for arbitrary stationary Regge metrics was verified. Curvature-measure convergence alone does not imply convergence of variational equations.

title: The Friedlander--Milnor comparison with finite coefficients
statement: For every finite-dimensional Lie group \(G\), prime \(p\), and degree \(q\geq0\), is \(H_q(BG^\delta;\mathbb F_p)\to H_q(BG;\mathbb F_p)\) an isomorphism? All coefficients are constant, and the topology on \(G\) on the right is its Lie topology. The corresponding statement for every finite abelian coefficient group is equivalent.
status: As of November 2026, retain C: solvable identity components, finite-component split surjectivity, and specified low-degree cases are verified in \citet{milnor1983discrete}; stable developments are recorded in \citet{friedlander2008conjecture}. The renewed 2021 preprint claim \citep{amrani2015friedlander} was located but not certified by an independent proof check. The 2025 publisher extract \citep{dranishnikov2025generalized} still labels the general Lie statement a conjecture. No accepted general resolution was verified in this audit.

title: Smooth modular-group coinvariants on the projective circle
statement: For every \(f\in C^\infty(\mathbb {RP}^1;\mathbb R)\), do there exist smooth \(u,v\) such that \(f(x)=u(x)-u(x+1)+v(x)-v(-1/x)\), with the two fractional-linear maps interpreted smoothly at infinity? The notebook also asserts density of these sums in the smooth topology; this is a separate claim.
status: As of November 2026, this companion proves exact solvability in \(C^0\), with a uniform norm bound and an independent proof audit, and gives an exact involution-averaging reduction of the smooth problem. Neither a derivative estimate nor a proof of the notebook's smooth-density assertion is supplied. No exact later resolution of the \(C^\infty\) equation was verified; the located minimal-leaf and invariant-functional sources remain related leads.

title: Uniform coordinate-product approximation of a Lagrangian plane
statement: For every Lagrangian \(L\subset\mathbb R^{2n}\), choose one line in each fixed coordinate symplectic plane so that their sum \(K\) satisfies \(\|P_L-P_K\|\le1/\sqrt2\). Alternatively, ask for any bound \(c<1\) independent of \(n\).
status: As of 11 November 2026: the sharp \(1/\sqrt2\) assertion is disproved here by an explicit real Lagrangian six-plane. A Fourier family forces any universal constant to be at least \(\cos(\pi/8)\). A fixed-dimension upper bound is \(\cos(\pi/(2n))\); the weaker existence of a uniform constant below one is unresolved by this work and no exact later answer was found in the documented search.

title: Geometric realization of compact-group weight multiplicities
statement: Express the weight multiplicity of an integral dominant representation as a quantization index, specifically a Riemann--Roch number, of the appropriate torus reduction of its prequantized coadjoint orbit.
status: As of 11 November 2026: established in the compact Hamiltonian setting, including the specified treatment of singular quotients. The notebook supplies evidence of a preprint by March 1982, before the 1982 publication.

title: Local extension of a two-form to an ambient symplectic form
statement: For a submanifold germ \(N\subset M\) with \(\dim M\) even, determine when a smooth two-form \(\beta\) on \(N\) is the pullback of a symplectic form near a specified point.
status: As of 11 November 2026: solved locally by closedness and \(\operatorname{corank}\beta_x\le\operatorname{codim}N\); see Arnold--Givental, Chapter 2, \S1.3.

title: Eta regularity without a bounding manifold
statement: For a self-adjoint classical elliptic operator of positive order on a closed manifold, is its eta function regular at zero without assuming any geometric filling?
status: As of 11 November 2026: established, in all dimensions, by Gilkey 1981 Theorem 0.1 after the earlier odd-dimensional APS theorem. The notebook’s possible reference to a more general nonself-adjoint setting is not covered by this formulation.

title: Spectral zeta constructions without self-adjointness
statement: Can complex powers, spectral zeta functions and a comparison measuring spectral asymmetry be defined for a nonself-adjoint elliptic operator on a closed manifold?
status: As of 11 November 2026: yes with spectral cuts admissible for both the principal symbol and the operator, together with resolvent hypotheses. This does not automatically establish the notebook’s separate normal-operator boundary index formula.
